sources.quote: Andreas Vesalius was born on New Year's Eve 1514 in Brussels, Brabant, into a wealthy family of physicians and pharmacists.
His early education at the Castle School of the University of Louvain included instruction in rhetoric, philosophy, logic, and classical languages (Latin, Greek, and Hebrew).
Shortly thereafter, his interest turned to medicine, and he went to Paris to study anatomy.
He worked there as a professor of surgery and anatomy, succeeding Paolo Colombo from Cremona.
The publication of Fabrica also helped Vesalius secure the position of Imperial Physician, in which he served until Charles V abdicated in 1556.
Vesalius published his dissections and sketches in the most influential text: De Humani Corporis Fabrica Libri Septem (The Structure of the Human Body).
His observations eventually led to the publication of 6 anatomical tables, the Tabulae Sex, in 1538.
Bruxella (Brussels) was the capital of Brabant, then part of the Habsburg Netherlands, and belonging to the Holy Roman Empire, with Charles V as emperor.
